title: King Oliver's band needs a tenor; Pete Jones finds Lester in Kansas City
summary: When Francis Whitby quit over paying for his horn, Pete Jones, business manager of the band, found Lester broke in Kansas City after hoboing back from Virginia, and brought him to Joplin.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah, he was with them. He played trumpet. They all came back to Kansas City. And when they came back to Kansas City, we had a tenor player with us who quit --
Francis Whitby. So Pete was the business manager of King Oliver's band -- Pete Jones. So they went up to Kansas City. Louis was up there, too -- they ran into Louis. Louis' band was up there.

Yeah. And they ran into him up in Kansas City. So Les saw Pete. He says, "Hey, Pete!: Said, "Man, if you ain't got a job for me, I'm gonna take one. I ain't workin'. I'm in bad shape. I just came back... I hoboed all the way back from Virginia." He hoboed all the way back to Kansas City. So he didn't have nothin'. Not that we (?). We just like brothers, you know. So when they went to Kansas City looking for a tenor player, we was in Joplin -- Joplin, Missouri. We were playing in Joplin. So the guy said, "Man, I'd sure like to find a tenor player." Because playing, and you've been used to having a tenor and they've got the two altos in the band, you miss it. So this tenor player, he quit. He quit because we wouldn't help him pay for his horn. I told him to go to hell. "I paid for mine, you pay for yours." So he quit. He went on back. He went on back.... They was after the horn. People come looking for him, and he wanted us to pay for it. He'd blowed off all his money, havin' a good time and ballin'... I said, "Hell, you didn't help me pay for mine." So I didn't give him nothin'. And nobody else gave him... So he left. He got mad and quit.

So we went to Joplin, and here they come back with Prez. Of course, they didn't call him Prez then, we called him Lester. We called him "Bub." "Hey man, what you doin'?" See, he already had been with this band once before. Some of these cats knew him. Cats said, "Man, we got it made. We got a tenor player now." Because this other guy we had, he wasn't bad, Francis Whitby -- nice tenor player.
